summary: Stephen A. Murphy works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his MA at SOAS University of London and conducted his doctoral studies under the supervision of Elizabeth Howard Moore.

Stephen Addiss (1935–2022) was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history who studied under Walter Piston at Harvard and earned graduate degrees from the University of Michigan. He held professorships at the University of Kansas and University of Richmond.

Stephen Batchelor is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under teachers including Geshe Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Rabten, and Kusan Sunim. He co-founded and led Sharpham College, served as a translator in Hamburg, and joined Bodhi College.

Stephen C. Berkwitz is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who conducted research at the University of Kelaniya and University of Colombo. He has served as an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Missouri State University.

Stephen F. Teiser is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religion who studied at Oberlin and Princeton under teachers including Denis Twitchett. He taught at Middlebury College before becoming the D. T. Suzuki Professor at Princeton University.

Stephen Fuchs (1908–2000) was an Indology and anthropology scholar who studied under Wilhelm Schmidt and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna. He founded the Anthropos Institute and taught at St. Xavier's College and University of San Carlos.

Stephen G. Covell is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his doctoral studies at Princeton University under the supervision of Jacqueline I. Stone and took up a post at Western Michigan University around 2003.

Stephen H. West is a sinologist who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Michigan. He served as executive director of the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies and held professorships in Chinese at UC Berkeley and Arizona State University.

Stephen J. Laumakis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under teachers including John Kronen, Ramdas Lamb, and George J. Tanabe. He serves as Professor of Philosophy and Director of the Aquinas Scholars Honors Program at the University of St. Thomas.

Stephen Jenkins is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Charles Hallisey. He has served as Professor of Religious Studies at California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt.

Stephen Prothero is a religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Yale and Harvard, completing his doctorate under William R. Hutchison. He became the C. Allyn and Elizabeth V. Russell Professor Emeritus of Religion in America at Boston University.

Stephen R. Bokenkamp is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied at UC Berkeley. He served as Associate Professor of Classical Chinese at Indiana University before becoming Professor of Chinese in Religious Studies at Arizona State University.
Stephen Suen is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at The University of Hong Kong, where he studied under the doctoral supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.

Stephen Wootton Bushell (1844–1908) was a sinology and history/archaeology scholar who earned his MD at the University of London. Early in his career, he served as house surgeon at Guy's Hospital and resident medical officer at Bethlem Royal Hospital.

Steve Odin is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology who completed graduate studies at Stony Brook University under David A. Dilworth and Edward S. Casey. He became Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi in 1982.

Steven Collins (1950–2018) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Richard Gombrich. He taught at the University of Bristol and later served as the Chester D. Tripp Professor at the University of Chicago.

Steven Heine is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Pennsylvania and Temple University. He held faculty posts at Villanova, La Salle, and Penn State, before becoming a professor at Florida International University in 1997.

Steven Lindquist is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Texas at Austin under Patrick Olivelle, alongside traditional teachers in India. He holds a post at Concordia University.

Steven Lukes is a sociologist and philosopher who studied at Oxford under E. E. Evans-Pritchard. He held posts at Balliol College, Oxford, the European University Institute, the University of Florence, the University of Siena, LSE, and New York University.

Steven Neal Weinberger is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his BA at Amherst and his MA and PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later serving on the faculty there.
